sentences.text: This animal was an ancient relative of crocodiles known as a thalattosuchian crocodilomorph.
Its most notable feature was a very long and narrow snout that closely resembled that of modern fish-eating crocodiles.
The creature possessed sixty-six teeth in total, with thirty-three located in each upper and lower jaw.
The genus was first described by the scientist Lortet in the year 1892.
Scientists place this animal in the unranked order Mesoeucrocodylia, the suborder Thalattosuchia, and the family Teleosauridae.
However, some databases list the family Gavialidae as the parent group for this genus.
Fossil remains have been discovered in France within rocks from the Bathonian epoch of the Middle Jurassic.
This species lived specifically between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago.
A conflict exists regarding the authority of the name, as the Paleobiology Database attributes it to Jourdan in 1892 instead of Lortet.
Despite the snout resemblance, this animal was not closely related to modern crocodilians because it appeared before true crocodilians evolved.
